claim: Ubiquitination regulates many different cellular processes, including protein quality control, membrane trafficking, and stress responses.
source: Ubiquitination regulates many different cellular processes, including protein quality control, membrane trafficking, and stress responses.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about ubiquitination's regulatory roles in cells.

claim: The diversity of ubiquitin functions in the cell is partly due to its ability to form chains with distinct linkages that can alter the fate of substrate proteins in unique ways.
source: The diversity of ubiquitin functions in the cell is partly due to its ability to form chains with distinct linkages that can alter the fate of substrate proteins in unique ways.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ubiquitin chain diversity and function.

claim: The complexity of the ubiquitin code is further enhanced by post-translational modifications on ubiquitin itself.
source: The complexity of the ubiquitin code is further enhanced by post-translational modifications on ubiquitin itself, the biological functions of which are not well understood.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ubiquitin post-translational modifications.

claim: Serine 57 (Ser57) phosphorylation of ubiquitin functions in stress responses in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, including the oxidative stress response.
source: Here, we present genetic and biochemical evidence that serine 57 (Ser57) phosphorylation of ubiquitin functions in stress responses in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, including the oxidative stress response.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by genetic and biochemical data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Vhs1 and Sks1 are the first known Ser57 ubiquitin kinases in yeast.
source: We also identify and characterize the first known Ser57 ubiquitin kinases in yeast and human cells, and we report that two Ser57 ubiquitin kinases regulate the oxidative stress response in yeast.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data showing kinase activity.

claim: Two Ser57 ubiquitin kinases regulate the oxidative stress response in yeast.
source: We also identify and characterize the first known Ser57 ubiquitin kinases in yeast and human cells, and we report that two Ser57 ubiquitin kinases regulate the oxidative stress response in yeast.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by genetic and phenotypic data in the manuscript.

claim: Ubiquitin can be conjugated recursively at any of seven internal lysines or the N-terminus to generate polymers with distinct topological features.
source: Ubiquitin can be conjugated recursively at any of seven internal lysines or the N-terminus to generate polymers with distinct topological features (Herhaus and Dikic, 2015; Yau and Rape, 2016; Swatek and Komander, 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: PINK1-mediated phosphorylation of ubiquitin at the Ser65 position plays an important role in mitophagy by regulating parkin-mediated ubiquitination of mitochondrial membrane proteins.
source: For example, PINK1-mediated phosphorylation of ubiquitin at the Ser65 position plays an important role in mitophagy by regulating parkin-mediated ubiquitination of mitochondrial membrane proteins (Wauer et al., 2015; Ordureau et al., 2015; Koyano et al., 2014; Kazlauskaite et al., 2014; Kane et al., 2014; Ordureau et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Phosphorylation of ubiquitin at the Ser57 has been reported.
source: Phosphorylation of ubiquitin at the Ser57 has also been reported (Peng et al., 2003; Swaney et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2017), but the kinases that produce this modification and its regulatory significance remain unknown.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The kinases that produce Ser57 phosphorylation of ubiquitin and its regulatory significance remain unknown.
source: Phosphorylation of ubiquitin at the Ser57 has also been reported (Peng et al., 2003; Swaney et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2017), but the kinases that produce this modification and its regulatory significance remain unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field prior to this study.

claim: Oxidative stress triggers deployment and re-distribution of existing ubiquitin pools and induction of ubiquitin biosynthesis to promote survival.
source: Oxidative stress is highly damaging to the cell, triggering deployment and re-distribution of existing ubiquitin pools and induction of ubiquitin biosynthesis to promote survival by activating a repertoire of ubiquitin-mediated responses (Cheng et al., 1994).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: During oxidative stress, many proteins become damaged and misfolded, resulting in a global increase in K48-linked ubiquitin conjugation that targets substrates for clearance by proteasome-mediated degradation.
source: During oxidative stress, many proteins become damaged and misfolded, resulting in a global increase in K48-linked ubiquitin conjugation that targets substrates for clearance by proteasome-mediated degradation (Finley, 2009; Shang and Taylor, 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Oxidative stress triggers translation arrest.
source: Oxidative stress also triggers translation arrest (Grant, 2011), resulting in K63-linked polyubiquitylation on ribosomes to stabilize the 80S complex and the formation of polysomes (Silva et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Oxidative stress results in K63-linked polyubiquitylation on ribosomes to stabilize the 80S complex and the formation of polysomes.
source: Oxidative stress also triggers translation arrest (Grant, 2011), resulting in K63-linked polyubiquitylation on ribosomes to stabilize the 80S complex and the formation of polysomes (Silva et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Ser57 is the most abundant phosphorylated form of ubiquitin.
source: Since it is the most abundant phosphorylated form (Swaney et al., 2015), we examined the biological functions of Ser57 phosphorylated ubiquitin in yeast, aiming to identify and characterize the molecular events and signaling processes that regulate its production.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Expression of S57A or S57D ubiquitin did not affect growth at ambient temperature (26°C).
source: We found that expression of S57A or S57D ubiquitin did not affect growth at ambient temperature (26°C) (consistent with previous reports [Peng et al., 2003; Lee et al., 2017; Sloper-Mould et al., 2001]) or sensitivity to arsenate (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and consistent with prior literature.

claim: Expression of S57A or S57D ubiquitin did not affect sensitivity to arsenate.
source: We found that expression of S57A or S57D ubiquitin did not affect growth at ambient temperature (26°C) (consistent with previous reports [Peng et al., 2003; Lee et al., 2017; Sloper-Mould et al., 2001]) or sensitivity to arsenate (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Expression of S57D ubiquitin conferred sensitivity to hydroxyurea.
source: However, expression of S57D ubiquitin conferred sensitivity to hydroxyurea and resistance to canavanine (which was reported previously [Lee et al., 2017]) and thialysine (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Expression of S57D ubiquitin conferred resistance to canavanine.
source: However, expression of S57D ubiquitin conferred sensitivity to hydroxyurea and resistance to canavanine (which was reported previously [Lee et al., 2017]) and thialysine (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and consistent with prior literature.

claim: Expression of S57D ubiquitin conferred resistance to thialysine.
source: However, expression of S57D ubiquitin conferred sensitivity to hydroxyurea and resistance to canavanine (which was reported previously [Lee et al., 2017]) and thialysine (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Expression of S57D ubiquitin enhanced both long-term and acute tolerance of thermal stress.
source: We also noticed that expression of S57D ubiquitin enhanced both long-term and acute tolerance of thermal stress (Figure 1B–D) while yeast expressing S57A ubiquitin exhibited thermal sensitivity (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1B-D.

claim: Yeast expressing S57A ubiquitin exhibited thermal sensitivity.
source: We also noticed that expression of S57D ubiquitin enhanced both long-term and acute tolerance of thermal stress (Figure 1B–D) while yeast expressing S57A ubiquitin exhibited thermal sensitivity (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ser57 phosphorylation of ubiquitin promotes cellular tolerance of various proteotoxic stressors.
source: These findings indicate that Ser57 phosphorylation of ubiquitin promotes cellular tolerance of various proteotoxic stressors.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data showing stress phenotypes of ubiquitin variants.

claim: Wildtype yeast cells arrest growth in response to oxidative stress.
source: Wildtype yeast cells arrest growth in response to oxidative stress and activate responses that help cells cope with the proteotoxic and DNA damaging effects of oxidation (Silva et al., 2015; Shapira et al., 2004; Petti et al., 2011; Martindale and Holbrook, 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Yeast cells expressing wildtype or S57D ubiquitin arrested growth in response to moderate oxidative stress (>1 mM H2O2).
source: Interestingly, while yeast cells expressing wildtype or S57D ubiquitin arrested growth in response to moderate oxidative stress (>1 mM H2O2), cells expressing S57A ubiquitin were deficient in this response and only arrested growth in response to more severe oxidative stress (>2 mM H2O2) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Cells expressing S57A ubiquitin were deficient in growth arrest response to oxidative stress and only arrested growth in response to more severe oxidative stress (>2 mM H2O2).
source: Interestingly, while yeast cells expressing wildtype or S57D ubiquitin arrested growth in response to moderate oxidative stress (>1 mM H2O2), cells expressing S57A ubiquitin were deficient in this response and only arrested growth in response to more severe oxidative stress (>2 mM H2O2) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The failed growth arrest observed for cells expressing S57A ubiquitin correlated with decreased viability.
source: The failed growth arrest observed for cells expressing S57A ubiquitin correlated with decreased viability (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 30 min exposure to H2O2 (1.0 mM) resulted in an increased abundance of total ubiquitin conjugates.
source: We found that 30 min exposure to H2O2 (1.0 mM) resulted in an increased abundance of total ubiquitin conjugates (Figure 2C) as well as K48-linked polymers (Figure 2C–D), consistent with a previous report (Silva et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and consistent with prior literature.

claim: 30 min exposure to H2O2 (1.0 mM) resulted in an increased abundance of K48-linked polymers.
source: We found that 30 min exposure to H2O2 (1.0 mM) resulted in an increased abundance of total ubiquitin conjugates (Figure 2C) as well as K48-linked polymers (Figure 2C–D), consistent with a previous report (Silva et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2C-D and consistent with prior literature.

claim: Cells expressing S57D ubiquitin exhibited increased abundance of K48-linked polymers during oxidative stress compared to cells expressing wildtype ubiquitin.
source: Compared to cells expressing wildtype ubiquitin, we found that cells expressing S57D ubiquitin exhibited increased abundance of K48-linked polymers and decreased abundance of K63-linked polymers (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2C-E.

claim: Cells expressing S57D ubiquitin exhibited decreased abundance of K63-linked polymers during oxidative stress compared to cells expressing wildtype ubiquitin.
source: Compared to cells expressing wildtype ubiquitin, we found that cells expressing S57D ubiquitin exhibited increased abundance of K48-linked polymers and decreased abundance of K63-linked polymers (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2C-E.

claim: Cells expressing S57A ubiquitin did not exhibit a significant increase in the production of K48-linked polyubiquitin chains in response to oxidative stress.
source: By contrast, cells expressing S57A ubiquitin did not exhibit a significant increase in the production of K48-linked polyubiquitin chains in response to oxidative stress (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2C-D.

claim: S57D expression increases the production of K48-linked polymers by 39% during oxidative stress.
source: Consistent with the immunoblot results, this analysis revealed that S57D expression increases the production of K48-linked polymers by 39% during oxidative stress (Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a finding supported by SILAC-MS data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Oxidative stress induced an approximately two-fold increase in phosphorylation of ubiquitin at the Ser57 position.
source: Indeed, we found that oxidative stress induced an approximately two-fold increase in phosphorylation of ubiquitin at the Ser57 position (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Co-expression of ubiquitin with the kinase Vhs1 resulted in immunodetection of Ser57 phosphorylated ubiquitin.
source: We found that co-expression of ubiquitin with the kinase Vhs1 resulted in immunodetection of Ser57 phosphorylated ubiquitin (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Vhs1 is part of the yeast family of Snf1-related kinases.
source: Vhs1 is part of the yeast family of Snf1-related kinases (Tumolo et al., 2020), and additional screening revealed three other kinases in this family that phosphorylated ubiquitin at the Ser57 position: Sks1 (which is 43% identical to Vhs1) (Figure 3B), Gin4 and Kcc4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Sks1 is 43% identical to Vhs1.
source: Vhs1 is part of the yeast family of Snf1-related kinases (Tumolo et al., 2020), and additional screening revealed three other kinases in this family that phosphorylated ubiquitin at the Ser57 position: Sks1 (which is 43% identical to Vhs1) (Figure 3B), Gin4 and Kcc4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a statement about sequence identity between two kinases.

claim: Sks1, Gin4, and Kcc4 phosphorylate ubiquitin at the Ser57 position.
source: Vhs1 is part of the yeast family of Snf1-related kinases (Tumolo et al., 2020), and additional screening revealed three other kinases in this family that phosphorylated ubiquitin at the Ser57 position: Sks1 (which is 43% identical to Vhs1) (Figure 3B), Gin4 and Kcc4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Vhs1 and Sks1 exhibited a preference for polymers (tri-ubiquitin > di ubiquitin > mono ubiquitin) in in vitro kinase assays.
source: Using purified recombinant Vhs1 and Sks1, we reconstituted kinase activity toward Ser57 of ubiquitin and found that both kinases exhibited a preference for polymers (tri-ubiquitin > di ubiquitin > mono ubiquitin) although the activity of Sks1 was noticeably greater than that of Vhs1 (Figure 3C–D and Figure 3—figure supplement 4–5).
evidence: This is a finding supported by in vitro kinase assay data shown in Figures 3C-D and Figure 3—figure supplements 4-5.

claim: The activity of Sks1 was noticeably greater than that of Vhs1 in in vitro kinase assays.
source: Using purified recombinant Vhs1 and Sks1, we reconstituted kinase activity toward Ser57 of ubiquitin and found that both kinases exhibited a preference for polymers (tri-ubiquitin > di ubiquitin > mono ubiquitin) although the activity of Sks1 was noticeably greater than that of Vhs1 (Figure 3C–D and Figure 3—figure supplement 4–5).
evidence: This is a finding supported by in vitro kinase assay data shown in Figures 3C-D and Figure 3—figure supplements 4-5.

claim: Vhs1 is active toward linear (M1-linked), K29-, and K48-linked tetramers.
source: Analysis of linkage specificity in the phosphorylation reaction revealed that Vhs1 is active toward linear (M1-linked), K29-, and K48-linked tetramers, while Sks1 is active toward linear, K48-, and K63-linked polymers (Figure 3—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6.

claim: Sks1 is active toward linear, K48-, and K63-linked polymers.
source: Analysis of linkage specificity in the phosphorylation reaction revealed that Vhs1 is active toward linear (M1-linked), K29-, and K48-linked tetramers, while Sks1 is active toward linear, K48-, and K63-linked polymers (Figure 3—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6.

claim: Overexpression of either Vhs1 or Sks1 increased ubiquitin phosphorylation at the Ser57 position.
source: Importantly, we observed that overexpression of either Vhs1 or Sks1 increased ubiquitin phosphorylation at the Ser57 position (Figure 3E–F and Figure 3—figure supplement 7–8).
evidence: This is a finding supported by SILAC-MS data shown in Figures 3E-F and Figure 3—figure supplements 7-8.

claim: Vhs1 and Sks1 are bona fide ubiquitin kinases that specifically phosphorylate the Ser57 position.
source: Taken together our data indicate that Vhs1 and Sks1 are bona fide ubiquitin kinases that specifically phosphorylate the Ser57 position.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data showing kinase activity toward ubiquitin Ser57.

claim: The family of Snf1-related kinases in yeast share homology with the human AMPK-related kinases.
source: The family of Snf1-related kinases in yeast share homology with the human AMPK-related kinases (Tumolo et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: A subset of human AMPK-related kinases phosphorylate ubiquitin at the Ser57 position specifically on tetramers.
source: To test if human AMPK-related kinases exhibit activity toward ubiquitin, we performed in vitro kinase assays and found that a subset of this family phosphorylated ubiquitin at the Ser57 position specifically on tetramers (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is a finding supported by in vitro kinase assay data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: MARK kinases (MARK1-4) as well as related kinases SIK1 and SIK2 exhibit Ser57 ubiquitin kinase activity.
source: This activity was apparent in the MARK kinases (MARK1-4) as well as related kinases SIK1 and SIK2.
evidence: This is a finding supported by in vitro kinase assay data.

claim: MARK2 produces Ser57 phosphorylated ubiquitin in vitro.
source: Mass spectrometry analysis confirmed production of Ser57 phosphorylated ubiquitin by MARK2 in vitro (Figure 3—figure supplement 11).
evidence: This is a finding supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 11.

claim: MARK2 exhibits a preference for linear, K11-, K29-, and K63-linked tetramers.
source: Further analysis of MARK2 activity toward linkage-specific ubiquitin tetramers revealed a preference for linear, K11-, K29-, and K63-linked tetramers (Figure 3—figure supplement 12).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 12.

claim: Ser57 ubiquitin phosphorylation activity is an evolutionarily conserved function for a subset of kinases within the Snf1-related family.
source: Given that Ser57 ubiquitin phosphorylation activity was detected within yeast and human Snf1-related kinases (Figure 3—figure supplement 13), we propose that this is an evolutionarily conserved function for a subset of kinases within this family.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data showing Ser57 kinase activity in both yeast and human kinases.

claim: Yeast cells overexpressing VHS1 exhibited resistance to canavanine and thialysine.
source: However, yeast cells overexpressing VHS1 exhibited resistance to canavanine and thialysine (Figure 4A–B and Figure 4—figure supplement 3), reminiscent of canavanine and thialysine resistance conferred by S57D expression (Figure 1A; Lee et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4A-B and Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Overexpression of a catalytic dead variant (vhs1-K41R) did not confer canavanine or thialysine resistance.
source: Overexpression of a catalytic dead variant (vhs1-K41R, which harbors a mutation in the conserved ATP binding pocket of the kinase domain) did not confer canavanine or thialysine resistance (Figure 4A–B and Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4A-B and Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: The canavanine and thialysine resistance associated with VHS1 overexpression was suppressed in the presence of S57A ubiquitin.
source: Importantly, the canavanine and thialysine resistance associated with VHS1 overexpression was suppressed in the presence of S57A ubiquitin (Figure 4C–D and Figure 4—figure supplement 4), indicating the phenotypes are driven by the production of Ser57-phosphorylated ubiquitin.
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4C-D and Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: Yeast cells overexpressing SKS1 exhibited hypersensitivity to hydroxyurea.
source: We also observed that yeast cells overexpressing SKS1 exhibited hypersensitivity to hydroxyurea (Figure 4—figure supplement 5), consistent with the hydroxyurea sensitivity phenotype observed in yeast cells expressing S57D ubiquitin (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: The hydroxyurea hypersensitivity associated with SKS1 overexpression was suppressed in the presence of S57A ubiquitin.
source: The hydroxyurea hypersensitivity associated with SKS1 overexpression was suppressed in the presence of S57A ubiquitin (Figure 4E), indicating the phenotype requires Ser57 phosphorylation of ubiquitin.
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Δsks1Δvhs1 double mutant cells failed to arrest growth in response to oxidative stress.
source: Notably, Δsks1Δvhs1 double mutant cells failed to arrest growth in response to oxidative stress, a phenotype that could only be complemented by the re-introduction of both VHS1 and SKS1 (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The growth arrest defect in Δsks1Δvhs1 double mutant cells could only be complemented by the re-introduction of both VHS1 and SKS1.
source: Notably, Δsks1Δvhs1 double mutant cells failed to arrest growth in response to oxidative stress, a phenotype that could only be complemented by the re-introduction of both VHS1 and SKS1 (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The growth arrest defect phenotype of Δsks1Δvhs1 cells was suppressed by the expression of S57D (but not WT or S57A) ubiquitin.
source: This phenotype of Δsks1Δvhs1 double mutant cells was also suppressed by the expression of S57D (but not WT or S57A) ubiquitin (Figure 4G) suggesting that the growth arrest defect in Δsks1Δvhs1 cells is linked to a deficiency in the production of ubiquitin phosphorylated at the Ser57 position.
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Sks1 and Vhs1 are dispensable for production of Ser57 phosphorylated ubiquitin in the acute phase of the oxidative stress response.
source: While these results indicate that Sks1 and Vhs1 are dispensable for production of Ser57 phosphorylated ubiquitin in the acute phase of the oxidative stress response, we cannot exclude roles for these kinases during prolonged exposure to oxidative stress or the possibility that they contribute to the phosphorylation of localized pools of ubiquitin.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the SILAC-MS data shown in Figure 4H and Table 1.

claim: Ser57 phosphorylated ubiquitin and the kinases that produce it play an important role in several yeast stress responses.
source: The data presented here provide evidence that Ser57 phosphorylated ubiquitin and the kinases that produce it play an important role in several yeast stress responses, but the low stoichiometry of this modification suggests its effects are likely limited and localized in a physiological context.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The low stoichiometry of Ser57 phosphorylation suggests its effects are likely limited and localized in a physiological context.
source: The data presented here provide evidence that Ser57 phosphorylated ubiquitin and the kinases that produce it play an important role in several yeast stress responses, but the low stoichiometry of this modification suggests its effects are likely limited and localized in a physiological context.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the measured stoichiometry of the modification.

claim: This study reports the first Ser57 ubiquitin kinases.
source: To the best of our knowledge, this study reports the first Ser57 ubiquitin kinases, and the only known ubiquitin kinases besides PINK1.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the findings in the context of existing knowledge.

claim: PINK1 activity is tightly regulated and highly localized to the outer membrane of damaged mitochondria.
source: Importantly, PINK1 activity is tightly regulated and highly localized to the outer membrane of damaged mitochondria.
evidence: This is established knowledge about PINK1.

claim: Sks1 and Vhs1 phosphorylate a localized pool (or pools) of ubiquitin in response to stress.
source: One potential explanation of the genetic and biochemical data presented here is that Sks1 and Vhs1 phosphorylate a localized pool (or pools) of ubiquitin in response to stress.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: A localized pool of ubiquitin phosphorylated by Sks1 and Vhs1 is critical for the oxidative stress response but is not resolved in proteomic analysis.
source: In this case, we propose that a localized pool of ubiquitin phosphorylated by Sks1 and Vhs1 is critical for the oxidative stress response but is not resolved in our proteomic analysis, or only contributes a small fraction to a larger pool.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation to reconcile genetic and biochemical data.

claim: Complete ubiquitin replacement may exaggerate effects associated with physiological ubiquitin phosphorylation.
source: It is important to emphasize that such complete ubiquitin replacement may exaggerate effects associated with physiological ubiquitin phosphorylation, which occurs at very low stoichiometry (Swaney et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2017) and probably in a highly localized manner (as exemplified by PINK1-mediated Ser65 phosphorylation of ubiquitin on damaged segments of mitochondrial membrane [Pickrell and Youle, 2015]).
evidence: This is a caveat about the experimental approach based on known stoichiometry of the modification.

claim: Ubiquitin phosphorylation occurs at very low stoichiometry.
source: It is important to emphasize that such complete ubiquitin replacement may exaggerate effects associated with physiological ubiquitin phosphorylation, which occurs at very low stoichiometry (Swaney et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2017) and probably in a highly localized manner (as exemplified by PINK1-mediated Ser65 phosphorylation of ubiquitin on damaged segments of mitochondrial membrane [Pickrell and Youle, 2015]).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Ubiquitin phosphorylation probably occurs in a highly localized manner.
source: It is important to emphasize that such complete ubiquitin replacement may exaggerate effects associated with physiological ubiquitin phosphorylation, which occurs at very low stoichiometry (Swaney et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2017) and probably in a highly localized manner (as exemplified by PINK1-mediated Ser65 phosphorylation of ubiquitin on damaged segments of mitochondrial membrane [Pickrell and Youle, 2015]).
evidence: This is an inference based on the example of PINK1 and supported by citation.

claim: Vhs1 itself may be subject to complex phospho-regulation.
source: Interestingly, this analysis also revealed a number of phosphopeptides derived from Vhs1 within its kinase domain (Ser86) and its Ser-rich C-terminus (Figure 3—figure supplement 9), suggesting that Vhs1 itself may be subject to complex phospho-regulation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of mass spectrometry data showing phosphorylation of Vhs1.

claim: Differences in linkage-specific activities in vitro may underlie non-overlapping functions for Vhs1 and Sks1 in vivo.
source: These differences in linkage-specific activities in vitro may underlie non-overlapping functions for these two kinases in vivo.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the linkage specificity data.

claim: Ubiquitin networks play a critical role in the eukaryotic cellular response to proteotoxic stress.
source: Although ubiquitin networks play a critical role in the eukaryotic cellular response to proteotoxic stress, precisely how these networks are tuned to enhance protein quality control and other protective functions remain unclear.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ubiquitin networks.

claim: Precisely how ubiquitin networks are tuned to enhance protein quality control and other protective functions remain unclear.
source: Although ubiquitin networks play a critical role in the eukaryotic cellular response to proteotoxic stress, precisely how these networks are tuned to enhance protein quality control and other protective functions remain unclear.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Oxidative damage of DNA activates signaling and repair processes that are tightly regulated by K63 ubiquitylation and deubiquitylation activities.
source: Furthermore, oxidative damage of DNA activates signaling and repair processes that are tightly regulated by K63 ubiquitylation and deubiquitylation activities (Demple and Harrison, 1994; Bergink and Jentsch, 2009; Ng et al., 2016; Croteau and Bohr, 1997; Thorslund et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Ubiquitin networks regulate many cellular processes critical for survival during conditions of oxidative stress.
source: Thus, ubiquitin networks regulate many cellular processes critical for survival during conditions of oxidative stress.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on established knowledge.

claim: Complexity of ubiquitin is further enhanced by the formation of mixed and branched polymers.
source: Complexity is further enhanced by the formation of mixed and branched polymers (Ohtake et al., 2018; Meyer and Rape, 2014; Swatek et al., 2019) and by post-translational modifications that can occur on ubiquitin itself (Herhaus and Dikic, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Phenotypes associated with ubiquitin variants are likely to over-estimate the physiological effects of ubiquitin phosphorylation.
source: Additionally, such phenotypes associated with ubiquitin variants are likely to over-estimate the physiological effects of ubiquitin phosphorylation.
evidence: This is a caveat about the experimental approach based on reasoning about stoichiometry.

claim: Mutation of Ser57 may alter the biochemical properties of ubiquitin in such a way as to phenocopy the effects associated with kinase deletion and/or overexpression.
source: Furthermore, we cannot exclude the possibility that mutation of Ser57 alters the biochemical properties of ubiquitin in such a way as to phenocopy the effects associated with kinase deletion and/or overexpression.
evidence: This is a caveat about the interpretation of the ubiquitin variant data.

claim: The identification and characterization of ubiquitin kinases is critical for understanding the biological functions of ubiquitin phosphorylation.
source: Going forward, these limitations present formidable challenges for dissecting the biological functions of ubiquitin phosphorylation, which is why the identification and characterization of ubiquitin kinases is critical.
evidence: This is a statement about the importance of the findings for future research.

claim: Deeper characterization of Ser57 ubiquitin kinases will likely be critical to understanding how phosphorylation regulates the biology of the ubiquitin code.
source: Ultimately, deeper characterization of Ser57 ubiquitin kinases – particularly to understand their localization and regulation in the context of proteotoxic stress – will likely be critical to understanding how phosphorylation regulates the biology of the ubiquitin code.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions based on the findings.

claim: Yeast cells expressing S57D ubiquitin exhibited significantly fewer propidium iodide-positive cells after heat stress at 65°C for 5 minutes compared to wildtype ubiquitin.
source: Fluorescence microscopy and (D) quantification of cells stained with propidium iodide (PI) after incubation at 65°C for 5 min. Dead cells are stained with PI. Results are means (n = 3) of % PI-positive cells ± SD (error bars). Double asterisk (**) indicates p value < 0.005 using a Student's t-test.
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C-D.

claim: Yeast cells expressing S57A ubiquitin exhibited significantly reduced growth at 39°C compared to wildtype ubiquitin.
source: With a starting OD600 of 0.1, cells were grown in liquid culture (-URA synthetic medium) at 39°C and OD600 was measured at different time points. Data was collected from four biological replicate experiments (n=4) and the mean OD600 ± SD (error bars) was calculated for each time point. Double asterisk (**) indicates p value < 0.005 using a Student's t-test.
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Yeast cells expressing S57A ubiquitin exhibited significantly reduced growth at 38°C after 24 hours compared to wildtype ubiquitin.
source: Cells in liquid culture (-URA synthetic medium) were grown at 38°C with a starting OD600 of 0.1 and growth was measured after 24 hr of incubation. Values are means of OD600 from three replicates (n = 3) ± SD (error bars). Double asterisk (**) indicates p value < 0.005 using a Student's t-test.
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cells expressing S57A ubiquitin experienced a significant loss of viability during H2O2 treatment compared to untreated cells.
source: CFU count of cells treated with 1.5 mM H2O2 for 20 min. Untreated control was taken before H2O2 treatment. Data was collected for three bioloigcal replicate experiments (n = 3) and the means ± SD (error bars) were calculated. Double asterisk (**) indicates p value < 0.05 comparing untreated to H2O2 treated cells using a Student's t-test, which revealed that only yeast expressing S57A ubiquitin experienced a significant loss of viability during H2O2 treatment in this experiment.
evidence: This is a finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.
